claims.statement: For fixed selector F(T,p), independent-set states of a rooted ordinary tree admit an exact branch-product decomposition of ranks and w_F, with cross-branch dependence confined to selected leaves supported at the root; root-centered legal two-for-one switches couple exactly two occupied branch roots. This identifies a reduction route but does not establish weighted Hall feasibility or S(T,p)<=0.
claims.scope: Arbitrary finite ordinary tree and fixed selected-leaf set F; the decomposition is unconditional. The proposed universal deletion-plus-two-for-one weighted Hall theorem remains unresolved under the primary eligible lower-region hypotheses.
claims.reason: retained: the root-present/root-absent partition, rank formulas, fixed-weight formula including root-supported leaf tags, and exhaustive root-boundary switch cases check directly from the tree decomposition. The route supplies no weighted Hall proof or primary aggregate resolution, and correctly records both as open.

limitations: The universal selector-preserving weighted Hall reduction remains open for arbitrary rank-constrained cuts.
No primary aggregate proof or eligible positive-sum counterexample was obtained or replayed.
No exhaustive computation, imported theorem, or Lean build was used.
